questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements is/are correct a heuristic function that makes it ‘consistent’ (or ‘monotonic’)?
S1 : The heuristic function h(n) must be non-negative for all nodes n.
S2 : For any node n and any successor n′ reached from n, the heuristic function must satisfy h(n) ≤ c(n, n′) + h(n′), where c(n, n′) is the step cost from n to n′.
questions.solution:
(c)
• Stating that the heuristic function must be non-negative for all nodes, is not a requirement for monotonicity. So S1 is incorrect.
• A heuristic is monotonic if, for any node n and its successor n′, the estimated cost h(n) to the goal is less than or equal to the actual cost to move from n to n′ plus the estimated cost h(n′) from n′ to the goal. So, S2 is correct.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
S1 : DLS guarantees finding the shortest path if the depth limit is sufficient.
S2 : BFS always find the optimal solution, if the path cost is uniform across all edge.
questions.solution:
(b)
BFS explores node level by level. If all edge have the same cost, BFS finds the shortest path in term of the number of edges, thus ensuring the optimal solution.

questions.qtext: When performing variable elimination, which of the following steps is performed last in the process?

options.text: Marginalizing out all variables except the one of interest.
Combining all factors involving the variable to be eliminated.
Normalizing the resulting factor to obtain the marginal probability.
Computing the joint probability distribution of all variables.

questions.solution:
(a)
The final step in variable elimination is to marginalize out all variables except the one of interest, resulting in the desired marginal distribution.

Consider the following statements:
S1 : Gibbs sampling involves sampling from the full joint distribution of all variables.
S2 : In particle filters, resampling helps to focus on particles with higher weights and handle particle depletion.
Which of the above is/are true?
questions.solution:

So, S1 is false.
• Resampling in particle filters helps to concentrate on particles with higher weights and manage particle depletion. So, S2 is true.

Consider the following statements about systematic sampling:
S1 : If the list of the population is ordered in some way, systematic sampling might introduce bias.
S2 : Systematic sampling is particularly useful when the population is small.

questions.solution:

questions.solution:

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: In IDA*, the heuristic function h(n) must always overestimate the cost to the goal to ensure optimality.
IDA* performs worse than A* in terms of memory usage for large search spaces.
IDA* can revisit nodes multiple times due to its iterative nature.
The time complexity of IDA* is always lower than that of A*.

questions.solution:
(c)
• The heuristic function h(n) must be admissible (not overestimate) to ensure optimality.
So, option (a) is false.
• IDA* is designed to be more memory-efficient than A*, especially in large search spaces. So, option (b) is false.
• IDA* can revisit nodes multiple times because it performs multiple iterations with increasing cost thresholds. So, option (c) is true.
• The time complexity of IDA* can be higher than A* due to the need to revisit nodes.
So, option (d) is false.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements about Depth-Limited Search (DLS) is/are true?

options.text: DLS is a variation of DFS that includes a limit on the depth of exploration.
DLS is guaranteed to find the solution if the depth limit is set high enough.
DLS can be more memory-efficient than BFS when the depth limit is set appropriately.
DLS guarantees finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
• DLS is essentially DFS with a depth limit to prevent infinite exploration. So, option (a) is true.
• True. If the depth limit is high enough, DLS will find the solution if one exists within the limit. So, option (a) is true.
• DLS can be more memory-efficient than BFS, especially with a depth limit that prevents storing all nodes at once. So, option (c) is true.
• DLS does not guarantee finding the shortest path; it only explores up to a specified depth. So, option (d) is false.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following is true about the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) in Approximate Inference?
S1 : The ELBO is a lower bound on the log marginal likelihood of the observed data.
S2 : Maximizing the ELBO helps in finding the best approximation to the true posterior distribution.
questions.solution:
(c)
• The ELBO is indeed a lower bound on the log marginal likelihood of the observed data. This allows for tractable optimization of the variational distribution. So, S1 is correct.
• Maximizing the ELBO improves the approximation of the true posterior distribution by optimizing the variational distribution. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements about factors used in variable elimination in Bayesian networks are false?
S1 : Factors can be created by multiplying other factors together.
S2 : Factors must always include all variables in the network.
S3 : Factors are not affected by the evidence variables.
questions.solution:
(d)
• Factors can indeed be created by multiplying other factors together, as this process combines different probability distribution. So, S1 is correct.
• Factors do not need to include all variables network. Only include the variable that are relevant to the factor itself. So, S2 is incorrect.
• Factors are affected by evidence variable, when evidence is incorporated. It modifies the factors to reflect the observed values. So, S3 is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements about Uniform Cost Search (UCS) is/are true?

options.text: UCS is similar to BFS but considers the cost of the path when choosing nodes to expand.
UCS guarantees finding the optimal solution for graphs with varying edge costs.
UCS can be more efficient than BFS in terms of memory usage if edge costs vary significantly.
UCS can be implemented using a stack data structure.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
• UCS expands nodes based on the lowest path cost, similar to how BFS expands nodes level by level. So, option (a) is true.
• UCS guarantees finding the optimal solution when edge costs are non-negative. So, option (b) is true.
• UCS may use more memory than BFS if the edge costs vary significantly, as it maintains a priority queue of nodes based on path cost. So, option (c) is false.
• UCS uses a priority queue to manage nodes based on their path cost. So, option (d) is false.

questions.qtext: In an α-β pruning algorithm, which of the following best describes the purpose of updating the a value at the MAX nodes and the β value at the MIN nodes?

options.text: To maximize the number of nodes evaluated by the algorithm.
To minimize the number of nodes evaluated by the algorithm.
To ensure all possible moves are explored without pruning any nodes.
To determine if a node should be pruned or not.

questions.solution:
(b)
The purpose of updating α and β values is to determine whether a branch can be pruned, thus minimizing the number of nodes that need to be evaluated.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
S1 : The complexity of variable elimination is dependent on the order in which variables are eliminated.
S2 : Variable elimination can be used for both exact and approximate inference in Bayesian networks.
S3 : The time complexity of variable elimination grows exponentially with the number of variables in the Bayesian network.
questions.solution:
(b)
• The order in which variables are eliminated significantly affects the computational complexity of the variable elimination process. So, S1 is correct.
• Variable elimination is typically used for exact inference. Approximate inference methods, like sampling, are different from variable elimination. So, S2 is incorrect.
• The time complexity of variable elimination is generally exponential in the number of variables, particularly if the network is densely connected. So, S3 is correct.

Consider the following scenario:
In an A* search algorithm, the heuristic function is admissible. Suppose this heuristic is modified to + c, where c is a positive constant.
What impact does this change have on the A search algorithm?

options.text: A* may still find the optimal path, but it will not be admissible.
A* will still be admissible, but the search will be less efficient.
A* will no longer be admissible and may not find the optimal path.
The change has no impact on the admissibility or efficiency of the A search algorithm.

questions.solution:
(b)
• Adding a positive constant to the heuristic can affect admissibility by potentially causing overestimation of the actual cost. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• The change in the heuristic affects admissibility, not just efficiency. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Adding a positive constant c to the heuristic function can lead to overestimation, which can make the heuristic non-admissible and potentially affect the optimality of the search. So, option (c) is correct.
• The change in heuristic affects admissible and on also impact the efficient of the search. So, option (d) is incorrect.

Which of the following statements about Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS) are correct?
S1 : DFS can be used to find solutions in graphs with deep solutions efficiently if memory is not a constraint.
S2 : BFS requires less memory than DFS when dealing with very large search spaces.
S3 : DFS is more likely to get stuck in infinite loops than BFS if the graph contains cycles.
questions.solution:
(c)
• DFS is effective for deep solutions but can use significant memory for large spaces. So, (S1) is true.
• BFS generally requires more memory than DFS due to storing all nodes at the current level.
So, (S2) is false.
• DFS can get stuck in infinite loops if cycles are present, unlike BFS. So, (S3) is true.

MIN player is found with a β value of 5, what happens next in the pruning process?

Consider the following statements:
S1 : Rejection sampling involves generating samples from a proposal distribution and accepting or rejecting them based on a comparison with the target distribution.
S2 : Importance sampling requires the proposal distribution to be normalized.
S3 : Rejection sampling is more efficient when the proposal distribution closely covers the support of the target distribution.
S4 : In rejection sampling, the acceptance probability is uniform across the sample space.
Which of the above is/are false?
questions.solution:
(d)

• Importance sampling does not require the proposal distribution to be normalized. S2 is false.
• Efficiency in rejection sampling in proves when the proposal distribution covers the target distribution well. S3 is true.
• The acceptance probability in rejection sampling is not uniform but is proportional to the ratio of the target to the proposal distribution. S4 is false.

(a)
Monte Carlo sampling estimates probabilities by averaging result from random samples. For large models, achieving accuracy may require a huge number of samples, leading to high computational costs.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
(a) If a heuristic is both admissible and consistent, A* search is optimal and complete.
(b) A consistent heuristic is always admissible, but an admissible heuristic is not necessarily consistent.
(c) The A search algorithm is guaranteed to find the optimal solution, even if the heuristic used is not admissible.
(d) A heuristic that always returns the actual cost to the goal is admissible but not useful for reducing the search space.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
• A consistent heuristic being admissible guarantees that A* search is both optimal and complete. So, option (a) is true.
• Consistency implies admissibility, but not all admissible heuristics are consistent. So, option (b) is true.
• A is guaranteed to find the optimal solution only if the heuristic is admissible. So, option (c) is false.
• While it is admissible, using the actual cost as the heuristic function does not help in reducing the search space, as it doesn’t guide the search. So, option (d) is true.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement is correct about the Expectimax Algorithm in Adversarial search?

options.text: Expectimax is used when the game has a deterministic outcome.
Expectimax ignores the opponents possible moves.
Expectimax is useful with a probabilistic chance component and opponent behaviour.
Expectimax provides the same outcome as minimax when applied to the same game.

questions.solution:
(c)
Expectimax is useful in adversarial search when there is a probabilistic chance component and opponent behaviour. It accounts for randomness and the opponent’s possible moves where as in minimax which is used for deterministic games.
